publisher: Planning Department, Government of Telangana (prepared with the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Telangana)
title: Telangana Socio Economic Outlook 2023 (Annexure 17: Demographic Details of Telangana; Annexure 22: Literacy Rates by Districts, 2011 Census)
licence: Government of India / State Government publication; reuse with attribution to the source
method: Printed Census 2011 literacy rate for Telangana (source line: Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India), transcribed as printed from Annexure 17(f), PDF p. 272 (printed 268); cross-checked against Annexure 22 State row (PDF p. 277) and Annexures 18/20/21 counts.
limitations: Copy retrieved from NITI Aayog's NITI for States repository (nitiforstates.gov.in), not from telangana.gov.in directly. Figures refer to present-day Telangana: the printed 2011 population (3,50,03,674) is 190,304 lower than the 10 districts as constituted in 2011 in the Census PCA (35,193,978); a 2011-boundary calculation from PCA gives 66.46 instead of 66.54. Census literacy = literates aged 7+ / population aged 7+.

publisher: National Statistical Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India
title: Annual Report, Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), July 2017-June 2018
licence: Government of India publication; reuse with attribution to the source
method: Household sample survey (stratified multi-stage design; first-stage units are census villages in rural areas and UFS blocks in urban areas). Values transcribed as printed from Table (7), PDF p. 151 (printed A-13): literacy rate (per cent), persons, rural+urban, age 7 years and above (col. 6).
limitations: Sample survey estimates, not a census count: state/UT values carry sampling error that the table does not print, and small States/UTs (e.g. Delhi, Goa, Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, A&N, Ladakh) rest on small samples (the 2022-23 report prints under 100 sample persons for Delhi, Chandigarh and Lakshadweep in its state education-distribution table), so year-to-year moves of a few points may be noise. Sample: 1,02,113 households; 4,33,339 persons (all-India). Literacy is self/household-reported ability to read and write a simple message with understanding in any language, not tested. Not comparable with Census literacy (different method, reference period and population frame). No separate Ladakh row (Jammu & Kashmir includes Ladakh). Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu printed separately; omitted (no DH code).
